ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: Three identical planets, each with mass M, are located at the three vertices of an equilateral triangle with side length L. If each of them moves along the circular orbit circumscribed about the equilateral triangle under their mutual gravitational attraction while keeping the equilateral triangle unchanged, which of the following statements is correct ( )

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, three planets are located at the three vertices of an equilateral triangle, and the triangle is circumscribed by a circle, with the center of the circle labeled O. The dashed lines show the sides of the triangle and the symmetry line extending from a vertex toward the vicinity of the center of the circle O; the center of the circle O is located at the central position of the equilateral triangle. Then reason: Select the planet at any one vertex as the object of study. The remaining two planets have the same mass, and their distances to this planet are both equal to the side length L of the equilateral triangle, so the magnitudes of the universal gravitational forces they exert on this planet are equal. The directions of the two forces are respectively along the two sides from this vertex to the other two vertices. Since the equilateral triangle is symmetric about the angle bisector of this vertex, the resultant force of these two equal forces must be along the angle bisector of this vertex angle, that is, the direction of the median corresponding to this side. In the figure, the angle bisector of the equilateral triangle passes through the circumcenter O, so the direction of the resultant force points toward the center of the circle O.
